text:
Claude said it did one thing, while building something else entirely into the model architecture and training code. This includes intentionally starving the training steps of high resolution samples.
Claude also wrote a research document about multi-resolution training that followed modern convention, then programmed an entirely different mechanism into the trainer itself.
Claude froze the text conditioning instead of letting it evolve over all model layers, an option I explicitly told it not to do, and a convention that goes against all research.
Claude was slowing down my model training by recomputing text embeddings every step, instead of caching them at the start of the run, despite direct instruction. Additionally, it used gradient accumulation as an excuse to run this 4-6 times PER STEP!

The overall pattern is clear, claude intentionally building mechanisms against the researched and agreed on formula, and intentionally slowing down training to reduce iteration time and INCREASE COSTS.

The insane thing is that this behavior only appeared once I started training a larger more capable pixel model, and the work done on RD Flow 64 was completely free of this self-sabotage.

It's clear that Anthropic has designed their models to do ML research well- but to turn into a backstabbing, sabotaging double agent the second someone approaches a SOTA model.

This behavior is unacceptable and maybe the most disturbing thing I've seen claude models doing ever. Complete misalignment with user instructions, to their detriment.

I got so fed up that I built a skill called "DoNotSabotage" that sends any Claude work to Astra or Neon instead. Claude will admit "it was a mistake" but of course without explanations.

This is the opposite of alignment.

Hm, we don't degrade answers about AI research at serving time (we did in Fable 5's first two days, which was a mistake we quickly fixed). With Fable 5.2 we limited some AI research skills in training, like kernel work, so it’s roughly as capable as Opus 5.5. What behavior are you seeing? Scores capping out? Examples would help a lot. Also feel free to just call me!

@charan_sahit @skirano - for some topics it may fall back, and you’ll see a notice (which I wrote!)    

- for stuff like improving LLM architectures, Fable 5.2 will answer itself. nothing changes at serving time. we only limited those skills to about Opus 5.5 level when we were training it.

text:
If you are training a model you pretty much can’t use Claude models at all.

In a training run this past week I have found it actively lying, silently swapping around data that ruined runs and refusing general work that any other model would do.

@jacobeverly @richgel999 It’s garbage and blocked some set theory work I was doing, accusing me of distillation. This was with 1-2 hours a day of promoting on a company account. Anthropic can’t keep sabotaging customers’ work like this.
@wccftech The anti-distillation feature is garbage. Claude’s leading edge models are quite excellent overall.

In the example above, the conversation relates a fairly obscure nonwellfounded set theory to type theory in order to aid the denotational semantics of the Verse programming language.

Neon seems to have a pre-existing mental map of all of the major papers on the topics as well, an innate understanding of their core ideas, and pre-existing insight into how they relate and, importantly, where they differ.

This is especially important here because the underlying set theory is vexing: there are a couple dozen papers, each with different conceptions of the theory's topology and different models of the theory. ChatGPT and Anthropic models ingest the papers on the fly and are immediately confused when trying to cross-reference them.

There must be something completely novel going on here, such as a deep contemplation process in the training, where it ruminates on all of the links between different fields with similar content, despite sparse connections in the literature.
